steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud console
steps.quote: Sign in to continue to Google Cloud Platform
steps.notes: The console URL redirects in one hop to accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier with continue= set back to the console. The wall asks for email or phone, with a Create account link and Guest mode hint. No bot check and no cookie banner appeared. A Google Cloud project is needed after sign-in (see step 2).

steps.title: Create or pick a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.notes: Not captured in this run. The docs sidebar lists 'Create a Google Cloud project' and 'Enable Google Workspace APIs' as earlier steps, but those pages were not read. A first-time Google Cloud user may also be asked to accept terms, which would be a human step (legal_acceptance).

steps.title: Open Google Auth platform > Branding and click Get Started if it says 'not configured yet'
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Requires the signed-in project from step 1.

steps.title: Enter App name and User support email, then Next
steps.quote: Under App Information, in App name, enter an App name.
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Agent can prepare the values. The docs tip says placeholder information is fine before release.

steps.title: Choose the Audience (user type): Internal or External
steps.quote: Under Audience, select the user type for your app.
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. The support page lists User type as External or Internal and Publishing status as Testing or In Production, but does not define Internal. The scopes section says 'apps used only internally by your Google Workspace organization' skip further Google review, so Internal appears to mean your own Workspace org; confirm in the console. The 'human' actor here is a decision for the app owner, not a credential step.

steps.title: Enter a contact email, agree to the Google API Services User Data Policy, click Continue, then Create
steps.quote: If you selected External for user type, add test users:
steps.notes: Quote (about the follow-on test-user step) verified on the live page. The checkbox wording 'I agree to the Google API Services: User Data Policy' is visible in the screenshot. The docs also say the consent screen can't be removed once configured; that quote is verified under step 7.

steps.title: External only: add test users under Audience > Test users > Add users
steps.quote: Enter your email address and any other authorized test users, then click Save.
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. A 100 test-user cap in Testing mode was NOT found on either page and is not claimed here. The only 100 figure on the pages is the new-user cap in step 9. Related verified quote: 'you can't remove the OAuth 2.0 consent screen after you've configured it'.

steps.title: Data Access > Add or Remove Scopes (apps used outside your Workspace org)
steps.quote: Some scopes require additional reviews by Google.
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Scope categories table: non-sensitive needs basic app verification; sensitive adds additional app verification; restricted adds a security assessment ('Security assessment required' verified). Verified internal-app exception: 'use of restricted or sensitive scopes doesn't require further review by Google'. Which Gmail scopes fall into sensitive vs restricted is not on these pages (UNCERTAIN).

steps.title: Know the OAuth user cap and where verification starts
steps.quote: 100 new users in total, after the app presents the unverified app screen
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Also verified: 'The user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.' The table's Appeal column links 'Request verification for your app' (verified), which is where verification starts from the Audience page. The page notes verified apps still see the cap but it does not apply for approved scopes.

steps.title: Google Auth platform > Clients > Create Client, Application type = Web application
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. This page is not in apps.json; it was read as the linked 'Create access credentials' next step. Docs also say a separate client ID is needed for each platform (verified).

steps.title: Add Composio's callback under Authorized redirect URIs and click Create
steps.quote: Under Authorized redirect URIs, click Add URI.
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Value to paste: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (per Composio docs; copy the exact value shown in your Composio auth config, since some toolkits still show the legacy v1 URL). Google compares redirect URIs exactly, which is a general OAuth point not verified on these pages (UNCERTAIN).

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret into a Composio auth config
steps.notes: Not visible without signing in. Caution: the credentials page says 'Note that client secrets aren't used for Web applications.' (quote verified on the live page), which does not match the usual Web-application flow where a secret is shown. Check on first sign-in what the console actually shows.

blocked_at.what_it_asks_for: A Google account: email or phone, then password. Create account and Guest mode are also offered.

observations: Console wall reached in one redirect, with no bot check or cookie banner.
The Google Cloud console itself is a single-page app behind sign-in, so none of the real consent-screen or client forms could be seen.
Quotes verified on the live page: 16 of 16 tried (10 are step quotes, the rest are cited in notes).
No 100 test-user cap was found on the pages read; the only 100 figure is the unverified-app new-user cap.
